title: Cavity temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: Oven cavity thermistor reads out of range.
fullDescription: AEG built-in microwave-combi units display F1 when the cavity sensor reports an open or shorted reading. The microwave function is locked until the sensor is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: From the back, reseat the cavity sensor connector.

whenToCallPro: Built-in unit removal requires care; consider a tech.

faq.a: No, the unit locks for safety.

title: Touch key stuck
shortDescription: Control reports a key held more than 10 seconds at startup.
fullDescription: F2 indicates the touch panel detects pressure on a key for too long. Wet rags or objects on the surface trigger this.

faq.a: A wet sponge can register as a finger press.

title: Door switch fault
fullDescription: F3 indicates the microwave's safety interlock switches show an inconsistent state. The unit refuses to fire the magnetron until the switches read correctly closed when the door is shut.
symptoms: Will not heat with door closed

fixSteps.title: Inspect door
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the door closes flush and the latch hooks engage cleanly.

fixSteps.title: Replace switches
fixSteps.instruction: Replace all three interlock switches as a set.

whenToCallPro: Microwaves carry lethal capacitor charge; professional service is safer.

faq.a: Yes, the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge.

title: Humidity sensor fault
shortDescription: Cavity humidity sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription: Combi-microwave units display F4 when the steam-detection humidity sensor reports out of range. Auto-cook programs are disabled until repaired; manual programs still work.

fixSteps.title: Run steam clean
fixSteps.instruction: Run the cavity steam-clean program if available.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If F4 persists, replace the humidity sensor.

whenToCallPro: Built-in units are best handled by a tech.

faq.a: Yes, only auto programs are blocked.

title: Magnetron over-temperature
fullDescription: F5 indicates the magnetron's TCO opened due to heat. Common after long high-power use with poor airflow or a blocked vent.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 30 minutes for the magnetron to cool.

fixSteps.title: Service fan/magnetron
fixSteps.instruction: Call a tech to inspect the magnetron fan and tube.

whenToCallPro: Magnetron service requires capacitor discharge; call a pro.

faq.a: Yes after the TCO cools, but repeating F5 means a real fault.

title: Cooling fan fault
shortDescription: Main cooling fan does not report speed.
fullDescription: F6 indicates the main cooling fan tach signal is missing. Dust, a loose plug, or a worn motor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum and reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the fan cavity and reseat the plug.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the cooling fan if it does not spin freely.

whenToCallPro: Microwave service involves capacitor discharge; consider a pro.

faq.a: Only if the fan starts spinning correctly again.

title: Turntable motor fault
shortDescription: Turntable motor not detected by hall sensor.
fullDescription: F7 indicates the rotation hall sensor under the cavity does not see the turntable spinning. A jammed turntable, broken coupling, or failed motor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plate
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the glass plate sits properly on the coupling.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the turntable motor under the cavity floor.

whenToCallPro: Call a tech if the unit must be removed from the cabinet.

faq.a: Yes, until the plate rotates again.

title: Mains voltage fault
fullDescription: F8 indicates the unit measured supply voltage too high or too low. Brownouts or supply issues cause this.

fixSteps.title: Verify supply
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician verify mains voltage at the outlet.

whenToCallPro: Always use an electrician for panel work.

faq.a: No, microwaves draw too much power for a typical UPS.

title: Steam generator fault
shortDescription: Steam tank temperature or level fault.
fullDescription: F9 on combi-steam microwaves indicates the steam generator failed to reach temperature in time, often due to scale build-up or a failed water pump.

fixSteps.title: Run descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run the descaling program with AEG-recommended solution.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pump
fixSteps.instruction: If F9 returns, a tech should inspect the water pump.

whenToCallPro: Steam-pump access usually needs the unit removed.

faq.a: Every 30-60 steam cycles depending on water hardness.

title: Communication error
shortDescription: Touch panel and main board lost communication.
fullDescription: FC indicates the UI and main control board are not communicating. Loose ribbon cables or a failed UI are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the ribbon between UI and main boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the UI board if reseating fails.

whenToCallPro: Built-in microwave service is best handled by AEG tech.

faq.a: AEG does not field-update microwave firmware on these models.
